problem_type: Durable identity lost when a pending spend card is re-read
symptom: Switching approval mode or restarting could make an existing paid card disappear, while delayed actions could target a newer quote.
direct_cause: The read model reinterpreted draft state through a process-local approval-policy bus instead of reading the presentation that created the card; card actions also lacked a presentation epoch guard.
class_root: A pending spend decision must remain bound to the exact generation presentation and policy snapshot that produced it.
affected_population: Users with an unresolved paid generation card
Approval-mode switches during an active run
Renderer restarts and delayed card actions
entry_points: Desktop spend-card confirm, revise, discard, remaining, and remove actions
internal_only_reason: The presentation identity and policy snapshot are Nomi's internal production-run contract; no external standard defines their lifecycle.
invariants: Every visible pending spend card has a stable presentationId and monotonic presentationEpoch.
A card action is accepted only when quoteId, planVersion, presentationId, and presentationEpoch still match the current card.
A policy switch never rewrites an existing presentation's pending decision.

door_reduction.why_not: Presentation creation, pending-card projection, and action validation are separate ownership boundaries: collapsing them would reintroduce UI policy into the repository or make IPC actions bypass the shared stale-card guard.

generality_proof: All desktop card reads pass through projectPendingSpendConfirm/listPendingSpendConfirms and all mutating card actions pass through appIntegrationSpendConfirm's identity guard, so mode switches, restart reads, and delayed IPC calls share the same durable contract.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Assign a new durable presentation identity, epoch, and policy snapshot whenever the displayed plan changes.
Fail closed when an action references a stale quote or presentation.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Every channel forwards presentationId and presentationEpoch to the shared application integration guard.
Planning and presentation commands persist the approval-policy snapshot with the generation presentation.

recurrence.reason: Any future caller that derives card visibility from live policy or omits the presentation epoch can reproduce disappearance or stale-action behavior.

prevention.invariant: Projection and action validation use the persisted presentation identity rather than live approval policy.
prevention.failure_mode: Projection errors become visible identity-preserving error cards; stale actions return generation_presentation_stale without mutating the run.
prevention.strategy: Persist identity at presentation creation and require it at every action boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: The process-local policy decision bus was the competing interpretation path and is deleted; policy is now captured in the durable generation presentation.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls this invariant.

migration: Legacy runs are normalized on read with deterministic presentation IDs and epochs; new runs persist the snapshot at creation and presentation time.
residual_risks: A real Electron restart walk still needs final green evidence after the renderer card error state is exercised.
Independent acceptance by the L walk line remains pending until its receipt is available.
